body:
DESIGN ANALYSIS bd-01M166XWESBS1JZ5B38H0ZZ2DK: is "which words support this alignment cell" one compiled artifact, and who owns the recall-side trace? Design only, no code, no source paths reserved.

THE PIECES ALREADY EXIST, and neither side is missing data. Source side: NodeSummary.support: SpanSet, clipped by the reader horizon in view/visibility.scala. Recall side: RecallUnit.span: SpanSet into the transcript, plus text, function, proposition and evidence. The cell that joins them: AlignRef.Cell(unit, state), where the state carries the anchor. So the trace is a join over three objects a consumer already holds, and nothing needs inventing.

THE CRUX, AND IT IS NOT WHERE I EXPECTED. I went in thinking the question was "which module owns a join". It is not. It is that THE TWO SIDES ARE GATED BY DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING.

- The SOURCE side is gated by an EPISTEMIC HORIZON: what a reader positioned at this point in the story is allowed to know. That is ADR 0002's whole subject, it is implemented in visibility.clipSupport, and the failure mode is telling the reader something the narrative has not told them yet.
- The RECALL side has no epistemic horizon at all - a participant's transcript is not hidden by where a reader stands in the story - but it does have a PRIVACY boundary: pseudonymized text, reidentification keys held separately, receipts that must never carry raw material. The failure mode there is not spoiling a story, it is IDENTIFYING A PERSON.

Those two gates have different owners, different審 failure modes, different audiences, and different consequences for being wrong. An artifact that showed both sides would carry an epistemic horizon and a privacy boundary in one object, which is precisely the collapse ADR 0002 exists to prevent, one level up. So my answer to the bead's first question is NO - not one compiled artifact, at least not one that renders both sides.

RECOMMENDATION, three parts.
1. THE JOIN IS A PURE FUNCTION IN align, not an artifact anywhere. align owns AlignRef, already depends on recall, and already reaches NodeSummary. Something of the shape (cell, recall, view) => (recallSpans, sourceSpans), returning RAW spans with no gate applied and no text. It is small, portable, and has no opinion about who may look.
2. GATING IS THE CALLER'S, AND BOTH GATES MUST BE NAMED. Any surface that renders the trace applies the story horizon to the source spans (view) AND the privacy policy to the recall spans (interview/embed). I would want that stated in ADR 0002's new sentence rather than left to each consumer: a renderer that applies one gate and not the other is the likely bug, and it is silent.
3. SPANS, NOT TEXT. The function returns spans; resolving spans to characters is where privacy decisions live, so the portable layer should not do it. This also keeps the trace usable by storyatlas4s without dragging transcript text into a library that must stay liftable.

WHAT I AM NOT RECOMMENDING: a third view artifact, a new module, or extending CodexFlow to carry recall spans. All three put the two gates in one place.

RESIDUAL I CANNOT SETTLE ALONE: whether the recall-side privacy gate is a POLICY the caller supplies or a PROPERTY of the recall graph it holds. If a RecallGraph can exist in both pseudonymized and raw forms, then "which words" has two different honest answers for the same cell depending on which graph you hold, and the trace should probably say which it was computed against - a fingerprint, as HsmmResult already does for view and recall. That is a question for whoever owns the privacy split, and it is the one part of this I would not implement without an answer.

Chief: if this shape is right I will write it up as an ADR 0002 sentence plus an implementation bead, or hand it to whoever owns the seam. I have three candidates queued already and no attachment to writing this one.
